newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close firmer, focus on Astra.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close firmer, focus on Astra.

text.p: Jakarta shares closed firmer on Wednesday on the back of strong rises in selected blue-chips, with the focus on the country's largest vehicle manufacturer Astra International, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 2.52 points, or 0.44 percent, to close at 572.29 points after touching an intra-day low of 569.61 points. Gainers led losers by 68 to 42, with 44 counters unchanged.
"Local-led active buying is likely to continue on Thursday with speculation on Astra boosting market sentiment," said one foreign broker.
Brokers said overall trade was dominated by local investors while the U.S. Federal Reserve decision to leave interest rates unchanged had only a light impact.
Astra topped the active list with 10.1 million shares traded, gaining 25 rupiah to 3,750 rupiah.
The volume was boosted by cross-trading transactions of about 1.6 million shares and block trade transactions of about 1.5 million shares.
Brokers have ascribed Astra's week-long rise to rumours that a syndicate of Indonesian businessmen is planning a takeover of the company.
Tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna confirmed on Wednesday he had bought some shares in Astra but did not give details of the amount or price.
"The news led to fresh buying in late afternoon trading. It also led the market to speculate that there could be another buyer involved," said a foreign broker.
Footwear producer Ganda Wangsa was down 50 rupiah to 900 rupiah on a turnover of 9.4 million shares after rising to 1,025 rupiah on news that it was considering a rights or a bonus issue.
Brokers ascribed the fall to local-led profit-taking after the early rises.

Toll road operator Citra Marga was also actively traded. It rose 100 rupiah to 1,650 on a volume of 6.3 million shares on what brokers said was fresh foreign buying on perceptions that its price was cheap. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
